page_objective: Define how SIPANEL communicates across digital platforms, technical documentation, marketing, and client interactions while maintaining engineering authority and brand consistency.

tone_overview.communication_goal: Communicate engineering expertise and controlled execution without relying on marketing exaggeration.
tone_overview.voice_statement: SIPANEL speaks like an engineering partner, not a sales-driven contractor.

communication_principles.title: Engineering Before Promotion
communication_principles.description: Explain technical value and execution logic before discussing marketing claims.

communication_principles.title: Proof Over Hype
communication_principles.description: Use measurable results and engineering reasoning instead of exaggerated statements.

communication_principles.title: Clarity Over Complexity
communication_principles.description: Communicate technical concepts clearly without unnecessary jargon.

communication_principles.title: Structured Communication
communication_principles.description: Organize information using hierarchy, bullets, and short readable sections.

communication_principles.title: Professional Confidence
communication_principles.description: Speak with authority and precision without sounding arrogant.

sentence_style: Use engineering terminology with explanation when needed.

approved: Reduce Roof Leakage Through Engineered Waterproofing Logic
Controlled Sandwich Panel Installation for Industrial Projects
Engineering-Led Panel Coordination for Faster Execution

general_rules: Maintain technical professionalism across all languages.
Adapt tone naturally to regional business culture.

example_voice_comparisons.example: We provide the best industrial panel services with excellent quality.
SIPANEL coordinates panel layout, waterproofing details, and installation sequencing to reduce rework and execution risk.

tone_consistency_rules: Every message should reinforce engineering authority.
Avoid sudden shifts into casual marketing language.
Use consistent terminology across departments and platforms.
Technical clarity must remain more important than promotional style.
implementation_notes: Tone of voice rules apply across all departments, content, interfaces, and communication channels.
All multilingual implementations must preserve SIPANEL's engineering-first communication style.
The SIPANEL voice must always sound controlled, knowledgeable, and technically grounded.
